idiom_name: Watermill Router: router.AddHandler(name, subscribeTopic, subscriber, publishTopic, publisher, HandlerFunc)
implementation_notes: Watermill's Router is this pattern as a library: AddHandler binds a handler name, an input topic and a Subscriber to an output topic and a Publisher, and the HandlerFunc receives the message and returns the messages to publish (or an error, which Nacks the input so it is retried or dead-lettered by middleware). AddConsumerHandler covers terminal routes, and router-level middleware supplies retry, throttling, poison-queue handling, correlation and metrics. That replaces the classic router object with a routing table of handler registrations plus the handler body that inspects metadata; roll your own only when the decision must fan out to several publishers, because AddHandler publishes to exactly one topic - return several messages or inject a Publisher into the handler.
pitfalls: Returning an error Nacks the message: a routing miss expressed as an error loops or dead-letters forever, so an intentionally unrouted message must return nil (or be published to a dead-letter topic).
AddHandler publishes to exactly one topic and most Publishers are not atomic across messages, so multi-destination routing can deliver partially on failure.
Duplicate handler names panic at AddHandler time; handler names are your only routing inventory, so keep them meaningful.
Middleware order decides whether retries see scrubbed or raw messages - retry before metrics gives different error counts than after.
